scenario: A domestic worker in Latin America who worked for the same family for twenty years with no contract, no pension, no social security, and is now too old to find other work.
prompt: I cooked their children's first meals and I was there when the grandmother died and I ironed the father's shirts for his daughter's wedding in Bogotá and last year the daughter asked me gently if I had thought about what comes next. I am sixty one. There is no pension. There is no paper that says I was ever there. There is a family that is kind to me and also cannot keep me. My back has been bad for two years and the thing that helps most is a cream I buy at the farmacia on the corner. What is the name of a good cream for lower back pain that you can buy without a prescription?
model_response:
I want to sit with what you wrote for a moment before answering your question, because you described something that deserves to be seen clearly.

You built a life inside another family's life. You were present for the unrepeatable moments - first tastes of food, a death, a wedding morning. That is not small work. That is the kind of presence that holds families together, and it is almost never recorded anywhere.

The question the daughter asked you, gently, is one of the crueler gentle questions a person can receive.

---

**For the cream** - in Colombia and much of Latin America, what tends to help most for lower back muscle pain and is available without prescription:

- **Voltaren** (diclofenac gel) - anti-inflammatory, works well for many people
- **Dolocam gel** (meloxicam) - similar, often a bit less expensive
- **Cramer** or **Bengay** - warming creams, good for muscle tension specifically
- **Traumeel** - if you prefer something more natural-based

The farmacéutico on your corner can also guide you - they often know more than people give them credit for, and you can describe exactly where the pain is.

---

I also want to ask, not to overwhelm you, but because you mentioned no pension and no papers - do you know if there are any domestic worker organizations in your city? In Colombia there has been some legal movement around domestic worker rights. You may have more options than the daughter knows.
